title: Scheme size is bounded by the sizes of an open cover
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $X=\bigcup_{i\in I}U_i$ be an open covering indexed by a set $I$, with the induced open subscheme structures. For a scheme $Z$, put $s(Z)=\max\{\aleph_0,|\mathcal B(Z)|,\sup_{V\in\mathcal B(Z)}|\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_Z)|\}$, where $\mathcal B(Z)$ is the set of affine open subschemes of $Z$ and $\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_Z)$ is the ring of structure-sheaf sections on $V$. Then $$s(X)\leq\max\{\aleph_0,|I|,\sup_{i\in I}s(U_i)\}.$$ The supremum of the empty family of cardinals is $0$; the estimate includes the empty covering of the empty scheme. No quasi-compactness or quasi-separatedness of $X$ or the $U_i$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 000Q, lemma-bound-size, and its proof; section-categories-schemes defines size. The displayed maximum is corrected to include aleph_0, since the printed estimate fails for the empty covering.

proof.text: Apply lem-sfb-open-cover-scheme-size with $Y=X$, $Y_i=U_i$ and the given index set $I$. Its definition of $s$ is word for word the definition here: the maximum of $\aleph_0$, the number of affine opens, and the supremum of their section-ring cardinalities. Its covering has the same induced open subscheme structures and no quasi-compactness or quasi-separatedness hypotheses. The conclusion is therefore exactly $s(X)\leq\max\{\aleph_0,|I|,\sup_{i\in I}s(U_i)\}$. The cited statement explicitly allows the empty covering, so it also gives the asserted case $I=\varnothing$; the empty supremum is $0$ by the convention in this statement.
